items.value: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — permaculture discourages monoculture, avoids the salinity build-up chemical farming causes, and depends on mulching
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: permaculture is built on polyculture and guild planting, while conventional chemical farming is dominated by monoculture. Statement 4 is correct: mulching is a defining permaculture practice (moisture retention, weed suppression, soil-building), and is optional in chemical farming. Statement 3 is wrong the way round — permaculture's mulching, swales and water-harvesting make it well suited to semi-arid regions, whereas chemical farming there depends on heavy irrigation. Statement 2 is the judgement call: chemical fertiliser residues combined with irrigation are a classic cause of secondary salinisation, which permaculture's organic, low-input regime avoids; and once 1 and 4 are accepted, B is the only option containing both.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct — palm oil is used in cosmetics and can yield biodiesel, but the oil palm is native to West Africa, not Southeast Asia
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is false: the oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) is native to West and Central Africa; Indonesia and Malaysia are today's largest producers but are not its native range. Statement 2 is correct — palm oil and its derivatives are standard raw materials in soaps, lipsticks and perfumery. Statement 3 is correct — palm oil is a major biodiesel feedstock. Since statement 1 fails, every option containing it (A, C, D) is eliminated.

items.value: The Chenab — it receives the Jhelum, Ravi and Sutlej and the combined stream meets the Indus
items.reasoning: The Jhelum joins the Chenab at Trimmu and the Ravi joins it further downstream; the Sutlej (having already absorbed the Beas) then merges with the Chenab, and the combined river reaches the Indus at Mithankot. So of the four named rivers, three pour into the Chenab. The Jhelum and Ravi are clearly tributaries and cannot be the collector; the Sutlej cannot be either, because neither the Jhelum nor the Ravi flows into it.

items.value: Saline lakes — the salt lakes of the Rajasthan (Nagaur/Sambhar) belt
items.reasoning: Didwana, Kuchaman, Sargol and Khatu are inland salt lakes in the semi-arid Nagaur–Sambhar tract of Rajasthan, worked for common salt. They are inland and far from the coast, which rules out mangrove areas; they lie in a hot desert-margin region, which rules out glaciers; and they are salt-production sites rather than designated wetlands of international importance.

items.value: The Nagavali and the Vamsadhara rise in the Eastern Ghats
items.reasoning: The Nagavali and Vamsadhara both rise in the Eastern Ghats of southern Odisha (Kalahandi–Rayagada) and flow south-east into the Bay of Bengal through north Andhra Pradesh. The Brahmani is formed by the union of the Sankh and South Koel and rises in the Chotanagpur plateau, and the Subarnarekha also rises on the Chotanagpur plateau near Ranchi — neither originates in the Eastern Ghats.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct — licences come from the International Seabed Authority, not the Global Ocean Commission
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is false: exploration and mining rights in the international seabed Area are granted by the International Seabed Authority, a UNCLOS body; the Global Ocean Commission was a short-lived independent advocacy initiative with no licensing power. Statement 2 is correct — India holds ISA contracts for polymetallic nodules in the Central Indian Ocean Basin and for polymetallic sulphides on the Indian Ocean ridges. Statement 3 is correct — rare earth elements occur in deep-sea muds and in the crusts and nodules of the international seabed.

items.value: Sugarcane — it consumes far more water per unit of produce than the alternatives
items.reasoning: Sugarcane is a long-duration, high-biomass crop needing roughly 1,500–2,500 mm of water per season, and is the standard example of a water-guzzling crop in Indian irrigation policy. Pearl millet and red gram are drought-hardy dryland crops grown largely on residual moisture, and sunflower has a moderate, much shorter water demand. 'Least water-efficient' means most water per unit output, which is sugarcane.

items.value: Both statements are correct — trade winds warm the western tropical oceans, westerlies warm the eastern temperate oceans
items.reasoning: In the tropics the trade winds blow from east to west and drag warm surface water westward, piling up warm pools on the western side (for example the western Pacific warm pool) while cold upwelling keeps the eastern margins cool off Peru and Namibia — so statement 1 holds. In the temperate belt the prevailing westerlies drive warm water eastward, which is why the North Atlantic Drift makes the eastern Atlantic and north-west Europe far milder than the western side at the same latitude — so statement 2 holds.

items.value: All three statements are correct — the Climate-Smart Village approach is a CCAFS project, CCAFS runs under CGIAR (headquartered in Montpellier, France), and ICRISAT is a CGIAR centre
items.reasoning: The Climate-Smart Village model was developed and piloted in India under the CGIAR research programme on Climate Change, Agriculture and Food Security, so statement 1 is correct. CCAFS is one of the CGIAR research programmes and the CGIAR System Organization is headquartered at Montpellier, France, so statement 2 is correct. ICRISAT, with its headquarters at Patancheru near Hyderabad, is one of the CGIAR research centres, so statement 3 is correct.

items.value: Tropical rain forest
items.reasoning: Rapid litter decomposition leaving a nearly bare soil surface, plus a flora dominated by lianas that climb to the canopy and by epiphytes rooted on upper branches, are diagnostic of the warm, humid, closed-canopy tropical rain forest. Coniferous forests accumulate thick slow-rotting needle litter; dry deciduous forests have a marked leafless season and little epiphytic growth; mangroves are halophytic, waterlogged and dominated by stilt-rooted trees rather than climbers and epiphytes.

items.value: Fire, grazing herbivores and seasonal rainfall keep tree cover in check in savannahs
items.reasoning: Recurrent dry-season fire kills tree seedlings while grasses resprout from underground buds; browsing and grazing herbivores suppress woody regeneration; and a strongly seasonal rainfall regime with a long dry period gives deep-rooted grasses the advantage over trees. These three are the standard maintenance mechanisms of the savannah biome. Soil properties and termite activity do influence savannah structure locally, which makes this item genuinely arguable — but they are secondary to the fire–herbivory–seasonality triad, and no option offers all five factors.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — polar ice and glaciers exceed groundwater, but rivers and lakes hold far less than groundwater
items.reasoning: Of the Earth's fresh water, ice caps and glaciers hold roughly two-thirds and groundwater roughly one-third, so statement 2 is correct. Rivers and lakes together account for well under one percent of fresh water — orders of magnitude less than groundwater — so statement 1 is false.

items.value: Statements 3, 4 and 5 are correct; moringa is not a legume and tamarind is not endemic to South Asia
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is false: moringa belongs to the family Moringaceae, not to the legume family. Statement 2 is false: tamarind is native to tropical Africa and was introduced into South Asia long ago, so it is naturalised rather than endemic. Statement 3 is correct — tamarind is gathered largely from forests and is notified as a minor forest produce. Statement 4 is correct — India exports both tamarind and moringa seed. Statement 5 is correct — moringa seed oil is a well-studied biodiesel feedstock and tamarind kernel oil has also been trialled for the purpose.

items.value: Fissure volcanic rock — the Deccan Trap basalts
items.reasoning: Black cotton soil, or regur, is the residual soil of the Deccan Trap country of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, produced by the in-situ weathering of basaltic lava erupted through fissure eruptions. Its clay content and high iron and magnesium reflect that basaltic parent material. Granite and schist weather to red and lateritic soils, shale and limestone to different residual soils, and brown forest soil is a soil type rather than a parent rock.

items.value: Both statements are correct — recombinant vector vaccines are made by genetic engineering and use both bacterial and viral vectors
items.reasoning: A recombinant vector vaccine is made by inserting the gene for a pathogen's antigen into a harmless carrier organism, which is by definition genetic engineering, so statement 1 is correct. Both viral vectors, such as adenovirus and vesicular stomatitis virus, and bacterial vectors, such as attenuated Salmonella and BCG, are in use as carriers, so statement 2 is correct.

items.value: Both statements are correct — mitochondrial replacement can be done before or after fertilisation, and mitochondria are inherited from the mother
items.reasoning: Mitochondrial replacement therapy has two forms: maternal spindle transfer, done on the unfertilised egg before in-vitro fertilisation, and pronuclear transfer, done on the zygote after fertilisation — so statement 1 is correct. Mitochondria in the embryo come from the egg cytoplasm, and the few paternal mitochondria that enter with the sperm are destroyed, so mitochondrial DNA and the disorders it carries pass down the maternal line only, making statement 2 correct.

items.value: Developing genetically modified crop plants — the Bt cotton events
items.reasoning: Bollgard I and Bollgard II are transgenic cotton technologies carrying insecticidal genes from Bacillus thuringiensis — Cry1Ac in the first and Cry1Ac plus Cry2Ab in the second — for resistance to bollworms. They are genetic-modification events in a crop plant, not a tissue-culture propagation method, a growth-regulator product, or a biofertiliser.

items.value: Only the area of the vent hole and the weight of the lid/regulator matter; flame temperature does not
items.reasoning: Steam escapes only when its pressure lifts the weight on the vent, so the operating pressure is fixed by that weight divided by the area of the hole; the boiling point, and hence the cooking temperature, follows from that pressure. A hotter flame merely raises steam faster and makes the vent release more often — it cannot push the temperature past the pressure-set boiling point — so statement 2 is wrong, leaving statements 1 and 3.

items.value: Only bacteria and fungi can be grown in artificial media; viruses cannot
items.reasoning: Bacteria and fungi are free-living organisms with their own metabolic machinery and grow readily on nutrient agar, Sabouraud medium and similar synthetic media. Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites with no ribosomes or metabolism of their own and can multiply only inside a living host cell, so they are cultivated in cell cultures, embryonated eggs or animals — never in a cell-free artificial medium.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — adenovirus causes some common colds and HIV is a retrovirus, but the genome descriptions in statement 1 are wrong
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong twice over: adenoviruses have a double-stranded DNA genome, not single-stranded, and retroviruses carry a single-stranded RNA genome which they reverse-transcribe into DNA after entering the host cell. Statement 2 is correct: adenoviruses are among the agents that cause common colds and respiratory infections, and AIDS is caused by HIV, a retrovirus.

items.value: Because the water molecule is dipolar (polar) in nature
items.reasoning: The bent geometry of the water molecule and the electronegativity difference between oxygen and hydrogen give it a permanent dipole, so its partially negative oxygen surrounds cations and its partially positive hydrogens surround anions, pulling ionic and polar solutes into solution. This is why water is called the universal solvent. Thermal conductivity and specific heat capacity describe how water handles heat, not how it solvates solutes, and simply being an oxide of hydrogen says nothing about solvent power.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; sodium lamps do not outlast LEDs
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: a sodium lamp radiates in all directions and needs reflectors to aim the light downward, whereas an LED is inherently directional. Statement 3 is correct: low-pressure sodium light is essentially monochromatic yellow with very poor colour rendering, while LEDs can be tuned across the spectrum and give far better colour rendering on streets. Statement 2 is the wrong way round — LED street lights are rated for roughly 50,000 hours or more against about 20,000–24,000 for high-pressure sodium, which is a main reason for the switch to LEDs.

items.value: Spread of viral diseases — ACE2 is the cell-surface receptor the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds
items.reasoning: Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 is a membrane protein of lung, gut and vascular cells that normally regulates blood pressure through the renin–angiotensin system, and it is the receptor by which SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 enter human cells. Its distribution therefore explains the tissue tropism and spread of COVID-19. It has nothing to do with transgenes in crops, with satellite navigation, or with wildlife telemetry.

items.value: Polycarbonate
items.reasoning: Bisphenol A is a monomer polymerised with phosgene to make polycarbonate, and it is also a building block of epoxy resins used to line food and beverage cans. Its leaching from polycarbonate bottles and can linings is the source of the health concern. Low-density polyethylene and polyvinyl chloride are made from ethylene and vinyl chloride respectively, and polyethylene terephthalate is made from terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol — none uses bisphenol A.

items.value: Toiletries — antibacterial soaps, toothpaste, hand washes and similar personal-care products
items.reasoning: Triclosan is a synthetic antibacterial and antifungal agent added to personal-care products such as antibacterial soaps, hand washes, toothpaste, deodorants and cosmetics, and concern over it centres on endocrine disruption and antimicrobial resistance from long exposure. It is not a permitted food preservative, has no role in fruit ripening (which involves ethylene-releasing agents), and is not a leachate associated with reused plastic containers, where the concern is bisphenol A and phthalates.
